hero.title: Focus in a calmer rhythm.
hero.description: Cadence is a desktop Pomodoro app built for task-based sessions, lighter transitions between work and breaks, and a cleaner daily flow without browser clutter.

items: Task-aware sessions

items.title: Does Cadence require an account?
items.description: No. The current product direction is local-first and account-free.

items.title: Where does my data live?
items.description: Settings are stored locally and tasks are persisted in a local SQLite database on the device.

items.title: Can I customize work and break durations?
items.description: Yes. Global settings exist, and active tasks can also carry their own timing profile.

privacy.title: Local-first by product design.
privacy.description: Cadence is built around local persistence for core functionality and does not require an account for the current product scope.

install.title: Installing Cadence
steps: Download the latest `.dmg` for macOS from GitHub Releases.
Open the `.dmg` and drag Cadence into your Applications folder.
Open Cadence from Applications or Launchpad.
install.gatekeeperTitle: Seeing "Apple could not verify this app" or "Cadence is damaged"?
install.gatekeeperExplanation: That's macOS Gatekeeper, not a problem with your download. Cadence isn't (yet) signed with a paid Apple Developer certificate, so Gatekeeper can't confirm who built it and shows this warning for every unsigned app — it doesn't mean anything is actually broken.
install.gatekeeperReassurance: The download is safe to open. Here's how:
gatekeeperSteps: Right-click (or Control-click) Cadence in Applications and choose "Open", then confirm in the dialog that appears.
If that option is hidden, open System Settings → Privacy & Security, scroll to the Security section, and click "Open Anyway" next to the message about Cadence.
You only need to do this once — future launches open normally.
install.homebrewText: `brew install --cask cadence` (after adding the tap once with `brew tap gutugaluppo/cadence`) installs Cadence without triggering the Gatekeeper warning above, since Homebrew removes the quarantine flag automatically. Never used a terminal before? See the full walkthrough below.

homebrewGuide.title: Installing with Homebrew — no command-line experience needed
homebrewGuide.intro: Homebrew is a small helper tool many Macs already have — it installs apps like Cadence for you and skips the Gatekeeper warning above entirely. If you've never used Terminal before, follow these steps exactly; the whole thing takes about two minutes.
steps: Open Finder, go to Applications → Utilities, and double-click Terminal.
A window like this opens — this is Terminal. Nothing you type here can break anything as long as you only paste what's shown below.
Type `brew --version` and press Return. Seeing a version number like below means Homebrew is already installed — skip ahead to step 5.

If it says something like "command not found" instead, visit `brew.sh`, copy the single install command shown on that page, paste it into Terminal, and press Return. It may ask for your Mac password — that's expected.
Click once inside the Terminal window, paste this line with Cmd+V, and press Return: `brew tap gutugaluppo/cadence`. Wait until a new empty line appears — that means it finished.
Paste this line the same way and press Return: `brew install --cask cadence`. This one takes longer since it downloads the app. When it's done, Cadence is in your Applications folder, ready to open.
homebrewGuide.pasteTip: Tip: pasting into Terminal always uses Cmd+V. Click once inside the window first, so your paste goes to Terminal and not somewhere else.

sections.title: Your first session
items: Open Cadence and the timer is ready to go — no setup or account required.
The reset icon restarts the current interval at any time.
The ring shows your progress, and the label under the clock tells you focus, short break, or long break.

sections.title: Task-aware sessions
items: The checklist icon opens a quick modal with your tasks — tap one to make it the active session.
The clipboard icon opens the full task panel, where you create tasks and give them their own focus and break durations.
Completed focus cycles stay attached to the task, so pomodoro counts build up over time.

sections.title: Customize your rhythm
items: The gear icon opens Settings: focus duration, short break, long break, and cycles before a long break.
Switch between light and dark themes, toggle sound notifications, and pin the window with Always on Top.
The app version is shown at the bottom of Settings.
